name: n4_users_audit
description: Audit the station's user accounts (station-audits S14), read-only and without a credential. One load of Services/UserService (each baja:User and its slots, two levels: an authenticator's own slots are never loaded), one of Services/RoleService and one fixed query of the /<station>/SecurityHistory Login records (where 4.x keeps logins; the AuditHistory does not). Fail closed: only fullName, enabled, expiration, lockOut, roles, authenticationSchemeName and prototypeName are returned; email and cellPhoneNumber show only "<set>" or "" under contact; every other slot (authenticator, password, permissions, vendor or dynamic slots) is never returned and is only named in masked_slots. Reply: users [{user, full_name, enabled, locked_out, expiration (null for never), roles, role_resolves, unresolved_roles, admin_role (a role that is baja:AdminRole or grants super), auth_scheme, prototype, last_login (null when no record), last_login_source (SecurityHistory, or null when it could not be read), contact {email, cell_phone}, flags (disabled, expired, locked, no_recorded_login, unused, admin, unknown_role)}], unused [{user, last_login}] (enabled users with no login within unused_days, claimed only when the records read reach back past the cut-off), unused_days, logins_since, counts (users and one per flag), masked_slots, notes, truncated (users past max_users) and elapsed_ms. A verdict the evidence cannot support is null, never guessed: role_resolves and admin_role need the RoleService; no_recorded_login means no Login record since logins_since (the oldest login record read; the SecurityHistory rolls, so an older login may be gone), and an empty history sets neither it nor unused. Read-only.

unused_days.description: An enabled user with no login in this many days is unused
